problem_motivation.content: Predictions of isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs lack experimental validation.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: the validity of these theoretical calculation methods to design the elastically isotropic and ductile BCC HEAs are still under debate and are lacking experimental validation

prior_approach.content: Prior work used ab initio simulations to design elastically isotropic HEAs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Recently, Tian et al . ( [7] ) suggested alloy design strategies to develop elastically isotropic HEAs (TiZrNbMoV x systems) using state-of-the-art ab initio simulations

rejected_alternative.content: Kroner's model fits better than Voigt and Reuss models.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: the Kroner model is in the best agreement with the experimental data for all temperature ranges, as compared to the Voigt and Reuss models

causal_claim.content: Atomic-size diversity creates severe lattice distortion and variable interatomic distances.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the random distribution of multiple elements with different atomic radii leads to a severely distorted lattice with variations in the interatomic distances along the crystallographic direction of the unit cells

mechanism_principle.content: Lattice distortion makes edge dislocations follow wavy paths.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: During the plastic deformation, the edge dislocation core can be deviated from their neutral dislocation planes, producing the wavy dislocation lines, which are attributed to the severe lattice distortion

hypothesis_statement.content: The study tests NbTaTiV deformation using neutron experiments and theory.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: we investigated the elastic and plastic deformation behavior for the NbTaTiV BCC refractory HEA at RT and elevated temperatures, using in situ neutron experiments and theoretical approaches

evidence_result.content: NbTaTiV is elastically isotropic at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Different from the conventional BCC alloys ( [11] ), the lattice strain evolution and measured diffraction elastic moduli indicate the elastically isotropic behavior at RT

evidence_result.content: The BCC phase remains stable through 900 degrees C.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The single BCC phase is stable up to 900°C, indicating the excellent phase stability at elevated temperatures

constraint.content: The alloy remains mechanically stable throughout the tested temperatures.
constraint.evidence_span: the present alloy shows good mechanical stability in all temperature ranges

contradiction.content: Temperature-dependent anisotropy is weaker than in conventional metals.
contradiction.evidence_span: it is found that the present NbTaTiV refractory HEA indicates the lack of strong temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation behavior at elevated temperatures, which is atypical elastic deformation behavior, compared to other conventional metallic materials
